arxiv-2101-05200.title: On the power of standard information for tractability for L 2 L_{2} -approximation in the average case setting
arxiv-2101-05200.creator: Wanting Lu, Heping Wang
arxiv-2101-05200.description: Abstract . We study multivariate approximation in the average case setting with the error measured in the weighted L 2 L_{2} norm. We consider algorithms that use standard information Λ std \Lambda^{\rm std} consisting of function values or general linear information Λ all \Lambda^{\rm all} consisting of arbitrary continuous linear functionals.

arxiv-2105-14145.title: Introducing the Voxel Interactive Contour Tool for Online Radiation Intensity Analytics (VICTORIA)
arxiv-2105-14145.creator: Elise Badun, Frédéric Tessier, Reid Townson, Ernesto Mainegra-Hing, Margaret-Anne Storey, Magdalena Bazalova-Carter
arxiv-2105-14145.description: Abstract In this paper, the Voxel Interactive Contour Tool for Online Radiation Intensity Analytics (VICTORIA) web viewer is presented as a solution to the issue of inaccessible, expensive, and insecure Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) and Monte Carlo (MC) dose viewers.

arxiv-2109-08298.title: Generating Concurrent Programs from Sequential Data Structure Knowledge using Answer Set Programming
arxiv-2109-08298.creator: Sarat Chandra Varanasi, Neeraj Mittal, Gopal Gupta
arxiv-2109-08298.description: Abstract We tackle the problem of automatically designing concurrent data structure operations given a sequential data structure specification and knowledge about concurrent behavior. Designing concurrent code is a non-trivial task even in simplest of cases. Humans often design concurrent data structure operations by transforming sequential versions into their respective concurrent versions.

arxiv-2111-14177.title: Evaluating Generalization and Transfer Capacity of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Across Variable Number of Agents
arxiv-2111-14177.creator: Bengisu Guresti, Nazim Kemal Ure
arxiv-2111-14177.description: Abstract Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) problems often require cooperation among agents in order to solve a task. Centralization and decentralization are two approaches used for cooperation in MARL. While fully decentralized methods are prone to converge to suboptimal solutions due to partial observability and nonstationarity, the methods involving centralization suffer from scalability limitations and lazy agent problem.

arxiv-2203-00523.title: Towards Creativity Characterization of Generative Models via Group-based Subset Scanning
arxiv-2203-00523.creator: Celia Cintas, Payel Das, Brian Quanz, Girmaw Abebe Tadesse, Skyler Speakman, Pin-Yu Chen
arxiv-2203-00523.description: Abstract Deep generative models, such as Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), have been employed widely in computational creativity research. However, such models discourage out-of-distribution generation to avoid spurious sample generation, thereby limiting their creativity. Thus, incorporating research on human creativity into generative deep learning techniques presents an opportunity to make their outputs more compelling and human-like.

arxiv-2303-08175.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ling-Hua Chang 1 , Po-Ning Chen 2 , and Fady Alajaji 3. arxiv-2303-10181.title: Operating critical machine learning models in resource constrained regimes
arxiv-2303-10181.creator: Raghavendra Selvan, Julian Schön, Erik B Dam
arxiv-2303-10181.description: Abstract The accelerated development of machine learning methods, primarily deep learning, are causal to the recent breakthroughs in medical image analysis and computer aided intervention. The resource consumption of deep learning models in terms of amount of training data, compute and energy costs are known to be massive.

arxiv-2403-19307.title: A Deep Redshift Survey of the Perseus Cluster: Spatial Distribution and Kinematics of Galaxies
arxiv-2403-19307.creator: Wooseok Kang, Ho Seong Hwang, Hyunmi Song, Changbom Park, Narae Hwang, Byeong-Gon Park
arxiv-2403-19307.description: Abstract We study the global kinematics of the Perseus galaxy cluster (Abell 426) at redshift z = 0.017 using a large sample of galaxies from our new MMT/Hectospec spectroscopic observation for this cluster. The sample includes 1447 galaxies with measured redshifts within 60′ from the cluster center (1148 from this MMT/Hectospec program and 299 from the literature).

arxiv-2405-20460.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by . arxiv-2409-02891.creator: Thomas Nils Nipen a* {}^{\mathrm{\textnormal{{a*}}}}, Håvard Homleid Haugen a* {}^{\mathrm{\textnormal{{a*}}}}, Magnus Sikora Ingstad a* {}^{\mathrm{\textnormal{{a*}}}}, Even Marius Nordhagen a* {}^{\mathrm{\textnormal{{a*}}}}, Aram Farhad Shafiq Salihi a* {}^{\mathrm{\textnormal{{a*}}}}, Paulina Te
arxiv-2409-02891.description: Abstract A data-driven model (DDM) suitable for regional weather forecasting applications is presented. The model extends the Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System by introducing a stretched-grid architecture that dedicates higher resolution over a regional area of interest and maintains a lower resolution elsewhere on the globe.

arxiv-2411-00674.creator: K. Kilmetis, A. A. Vidotto, A. Allan, D. Kubyshkina
arxiv-2411-00674.description: Abstract Numerical simulations have shown that the strength of planetary magnetic fields depends on the convective energy flux emerging from planetary interiors. Here we model the interior structure of gas giant planets using MESA , to determine the convective energy flux that can drive the generation of magnetic field. This flux is then incorporated in the Christensen et al.

arxiv-2501-06771.title: Modularity of preferential attachment graphs
arxiv-2501-06771.creator: Katarzyna Rybarczyk * {}^{\textrm{*}}, Małgorzata Sulkowska ⋆ {}^{\textrm{$\star$}}
arxiv-2501-06771.description: Abstract . We study a preferential attachment model G n h G_{n}^{h} . The graph G n h G_{n}^{h} is generated from a finite initial graph by adding new vertices one at a time. Each new vertex connects to h ≥ 1 h\geq 1 already existing vertices, and these are chosen with probability proportional to their current degrees.

arxiv-2505-16345.creator: V. Dolean, P. Marchand, A. Modave, T. Raynaud
arxiv-2505-16345.description: Abstract The finite element solution of Helmholtz problems near resonant or quasi-resonant frequencies poses significant challenges, as iterative solvers typically suffer from severely degraded convergence. We analyze the convergence behavior of GMRES applied to linear systems arising from such configurations.

arxiv-2508-07935.title: SHIELDA: Structured Handling of Exceptions in LLM-Driven Agentic Workflows
arxiv-2508-07935.creator: Jingwen Zhou, Jieshan Chen, Qinghua Lu, Dehai Zhao, Liming Zhu
arxiv-2508-07935.description: Abstract Large Language Model (LLM) agentic systems are software systems powered by LLMs that autonomously reason, plan, and execute multi-step workflows to achieve human goals, rather than merely executing predefined steps. During execution, these workflows frequently encounter exceptions. Existing exception handling solutions often treat exceptions superficially, failing to trace execution-phase exceptions to their reasoning-phase root causes.

arxiv-2511-06457.title: Inpaint360GS: Efficient Object-Aware 3D Inpainting via Gaussian Splatting for 360° Scenes
arxiv-2511-06457.creator: Shaoxiang Wang, Shihong Zhang, Christen Millerdurai, Rüdiger Westermann, Didier Stricker, Alain Pagani
arxiv-2511-06457.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shaoxiang Wang, Shihong Zhang, Christen Millerdurai, Rüdiger Westermann, Didier Stricker, Alain Pagani. Despite recent advances in single-object front-facing inpainting using NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), inpainting in complex 360 ∘ 360^{\circ} scenes remains largely underexplored. This is primarily due to three key challenges: (i) identifying target objects in the 3D field of 360° environments, (ii) dealing with severe occlusions in multi-object scenes, which makes it hard to define regions to inpaint, and (iii) maintaining consistent and high-quality appearance across views effectively.

arxiv-2511-22990.title: MIMM-X: Disentangeling Spurious Correlations for Medical Image Analysis
arxiv-2511-22990.creator: Louisa Fay (🖂), Hajer Reguigui, Bin Yang, Sergios Gatidis, Thomas Küstner
arxiv-2511-22990.description: Abstract Deep learning models can excel on medical tasks, yet often experience spurious correlations, known as shortcut learning, leading to poor generalization in new environments. Particularly in medical imaging, where multiple spurious correlations can coexist, misclassifications can have severe consequences. We propose MIMM-X, a framework that disentangles causal features from multiple spurious correlations by minimizing their mutual information.
